title: Bitcoin Drops Below $80K After Strong Jobs Data, ETF Inflows Collapse 76% In A Day
detail:
Bitcoin Drops Below $80K After Strong Jobs Data, ETF Inflows Collapse 76% In A Day
Anushka Basu
Sat, September 5, 2026 at 4:52 AM MDT 4 min read
BTC-USD
BAC
Trade BTC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bitcoin fell below $80,000 on Saturday after a stronger-than-expected August jobs report.

Nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000, tripling forecasts, and unemployment stayed at 4.1%.

Spot Bitcoin ETF inflows dropped 76% to $174.60 million on Friday, from $730 million on Thursday.

Bitcoin (BTC) fell below $80,000 on Saturday, down more than 1% after a stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs report for August rattled the cryptocurrency market.

On Friday, Nonfarm payrolls increased by 162,000 in August, more than triple the 53,000 economists had expected, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). Private payrolls were also much stronger than expected, with 127,000 jobs added compared with expectations of around 43,000 to 45,000. The unemployment rate remained at 4.1%. The BLS also revised up payrolls for June and July by a combined 55,000 jobs. 

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

Jobs Report May Not Set Fed Path

According to a Bitunix analyst, Bank of America (BofA) said before Friday's report that the jobs data alone may not be enough to significantly move current rate-hike pricing unless payroll growth is substantially below forecasts. 

But the bank pointed to the September 11 Consumer Price Index (CPI) report as a more definitive signal for the Fed's rate path, arguing that if inflation remained sticky even as the labor market became softer, higher rates could keep funding costs and pressure risk-asset valuations, including crypto. 

Analysts also said that the yen carry trade offered a separate channel for transmitting Japanese monetary policy shocks to the crypto markets, beyond U.S. data.

Garett Jin on substack.

On Substack, popular trader Garrett Jin said that Bitcoin came under pressure and was 'rejected brutally' at $82,500. According to the trader, if Bitcoin's price rises, more people who bought at higher prices could use it as an opportunity to sell, in turn creating additional selling pressure. According to him, more traders are betting that Bitcoin's price will fall, making the market likely vulnerable to a short squeeze. 

ETF Flows Reverse

On Thursday, before the jobs report was announced, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $730.9 million in inflows, the highest since February. However, net inflows into spot Bitcoin ETFs on Friday totaled $174.60 million, down about 76% from Thursday's number, according to SoSoValue data.

Thursday's inflow coincided with Bitcoin rallying to $81,000 on the back of comments from Fed Governor Christopher Waller, who said he was open to keeping rates steady if inflation continued to ease.

BofA lifted its Hormel Foods price target to US$27 from US$25 after the planned Ceratti divestment in Brazil. The firm points to improved earnings visibility and continued portfolio simplification as support for a modest re rating in the stock's valuation multiple.

BofA also cites cost deflation as a supportive factor, which it links to a cleaner, more focused portfolio that could make Hormel Foods' earnings profile easier for investors to assess.

JPMorgan raised its Hormel Foods price target to US$26 from US$25 and kept a Neutral stance. This indicates that some large brokers still see scope for incremental upside within a relatively balanced risk reward view.

Both BofA and JPMorgan maintain non bullish ratings despite the higher targets, which signals that large firms still see constraints on upside potential at current valuation levels.

The clustering of targets around the mid US$20s suggests expectations for Hormel Foods remain measured. Analysts appear to want clearer evidence on execution and growth before shifting toward more positive recommendations.

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Chewy (NYSE:CHWY) heads into its September 9 earnings report with Bank of America arguing that the beaten-down pet retailer may be approaching a better setup than its stock price suggests.

BofA analyst Michael McGovern reiterated a Buy rating and $31 price target, pointing to improving pet-industry spending trends and continued opportunities for Chewy to expand margins through advertising, healthcare services and automation.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with CHWY.

Is CHWY fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Net/net, we remain constructive on steady compounding earnings growth driven by margin expansion from ads, Health/CVC, & automation/AI, McGovern said.

The bullish call comes after a difficult year for shareholders. Chewy stock has fallen roughly 27% year to date, hurt by a full-year guidance reduction in June and concerns that consumer uncertainty could slow discretionary pet spending.

Wall Street expects fiscal Q2 earnings of $0.18 per share, representing roughly 29% year-over-year growth, on revenue of about $3.32 billion, up approximately 7.1%.

Bank of America sees some encouraging signs underneath those estimates.

The bank's credit- and debit-card data showed pet-industry spending growth accelerating from roughly 1% in Q2 to 2% in July. Separate Second Measure data also indicated improving momentum during July, potentially giving Chewy a better backdrop heading into the quarter.

That matters because investor sentiment has become increasingly divided. Bulls expect pet demand to recover as household formation and premiumization improve, while bears remain focused on slower sales growth and Chewy's market-share trajectory.

McGovern argues the recent valuation reset reflects macroeconomic weakness more than deterioration in Chewy's competitive position.

What Chewy investors should watch next

The September 9 report will largely come down to whether improving category data is beginning to show up in Chewy's actual results.

Investors should watch net sales growth, active customers, Autoship penetration and gross margin, along with management's full-year outlook.

Margin expansion may prove especially important. If advertising, healthcare and automation allow earnings to grow faster than revenue, Chewy could continue compounding profits even while the broader pet category remains subdued.

But another guidance reduction or signs of further market-share pressure would reinforce the bear case.

For now, Bank of America is betting that Chewy's 27% decline has created a more attractive entry point just as industry demand begins showing early signs of improvement.

title: Bank of America's new warning should concern stock investors
detail:
Bank of America's new warning should concern stock investors
Damilola Esebame
Thu, September 3, 2026 at 10:47 AM MDT 5 min read
^GSPC
BAC
Trade BAC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The S&P 500 has delivered double-digit gains in 2026, and the rally has outlasted every warning thrown at it so far. One of Wall Street's most closely tracked positioning gauges is now flashing a different signal.

Bank of America's proprietary Bull & Bear Indicator has remained in sell-signal territory since May 2026, with July weekly readings ranging from 9.5 to 9.6 on a 10-point scale, Business Insider showed. 

Those are the highest levels seen since 2021, driven by extreme positioning across hedge funds, fund managers, equity flows, and credit-market technicals.

"Extreme bull positioning says reduce risk exposure," Bank of America chief investment strategist Michael Hartnett said in a client note, Business Insider reported.

The signal does not guarantee a decline, and prior sell triggers have sometimes fizzled without producing meaningful losses. But the buyer pool has thinned enough that even modest earnings or policy disappointment can spark outsized selling pressure.

Bank of America's indicator hits 9.5 as positioning extremes spread across asset classes

The indicator blends institutional positioning, equity and bond flows, global stock-index breadth, and credit-market technicals into one composite score. When that score crosses above 8.0, the firm treats it as a contrarian sell signal for risk assets.

Fund-manager positioning reached the 99th percentile, equity flows hit the 93rd percentile, and hedge-fund exposure registered at the 83rd percentile in Bank of America's component breakdown reported by Guru Focus. 

Also read: Rare volatility signal prompts stock market alert from 43-year veteran analyst

Credit-market technicals also came in elevated at the 77th percentile, reflecting tight high-yield spreads and thin risk premiums across global bond markets.

A second threshold fired alongside the indicator, with managers cutting cash reserves to 3.5% of total assets under management in the August Global Fund Manager Survey, down from 3.6% in July and the sixth-lowest reading in the survey's history since 1998. 

That breaches Bank of America's 4.0% Cash Rule, a sell indicator that confirms institutions are fully deployed, with almost no dry powder remaining.

What 17 prior sell signals reveal about near-term stock returns

The indicator has fired 17 sell signals since its launch 24 years ago, giving investors a meaningful sample of post-signal outcomes to evaluate.

Global stocks, as measured by the MSCI All Country World Index, averaged declines of 2% to 3% in the two to three months following each signal, Hartnett noted.
